title: Spectro-temporal shaping of broadband optical wavepackets via programmable on-chip photonics
authors: Bruno P. Chaves, Jérémy Saucourt, Van Thuy Hoang, Alexis Bougaud, Yassin Boussafa, Erwan Ferrandon, Sai T. Chu, Brent E. Little, David J. Moss, Roberto Morandotti, Vincent Couderc, Benjamin Wetzel
abstract: The ability to precisely shape the properties of light over multiple degrees of freedom constitutes the foundation of modern photonic architectures. Broadband sources with addressable spectro-temporal content are for instance critical for applications spanning biomedical imaging, material processing, lidar, and ultrafast spectroscopy, but also key enabling technologies in quantum information processing, high-capacity communications, and optical computing. Yet, flexible and adjustable spectro-temporal shaping so far remains a significant challenge, as it requires the simultaneous manipulation of both frequency and temporal domains across broad spectral bandwidths and extended timescales, from femtoseconds to nanoseconds. Importantly, conventional approaches to spectro-temporal processing typically rely on bulky and complex optical systems that lack scalability and flexibility, ultimately hampering their utility for applications requiring addressable multiphotonic processes. Here, we present a framework for spectro-temporal wavepacket control over a broad bandwidth, merging programmable integrated photonics with high-speed optical characterization. Leveraging machine leaning for tailoring nonlinear pulse propagation, we experimentally report scalable and on-demand shaping of broadband ultrafast pulse patterns. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through reconfigurable power across 400 nm bandwidth with picosecond resolution, with promises for applications where precise control over light is paramount, in particular those needing versatile and controllable multiphoton excitations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, scalable platform for precisely controlling the spectral and temporal properties of broadband optical pulses. By integrating programmable photonics with nonlinear fiber optics and employing machine learning optimization, the authors can generate tailored ultrafast wavepackets on demand. This breakthrough overcomes the limitations of bulky conventional systems, enabling next-generation applications in quantum optics and advanced imaging.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving flexible and adjustable spectro-temporal shaping of broadband optical wavepackets for advanced applications like quantum information processing and ultrafast spectroscopy.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a scalable, on-demand method to tailor broadband ultrafast pulse patterns, achieving reconfigurable power control across a 400 nm bandwidth with picosecond resolution.
method: The technique merges programmable integrated photonics with nonlinear fiber propagation, using machine learning (ML) algorithms to iteratively optimize the input pulse to achieve a desired output spectro-temporal profile.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a programmable delay line (PDL) to condition the input pulse into a highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF) which generates a supercontinuum (SC). The output is characterized using advanced techniques like X-FROG.
key_observables: Spectrograms showing spectral and temporal content, and a Figure of Merit (FoM) used to guide optimization towards target spectro-temporal patterns.
important_parameters: 400 nm bandwidth, picosecond resolution, and the ability to control interpulse delays across hundreds of picoseconds.
main_assumptions: Conventional spectro-temporal processing methods are bulky and lack scalability, necessitating the integrated photonic approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup involving the PDL, HNLF, and characterization stages, alongside examples of tailored spectro-temporal wavepackets (e.g., DT2, OV4) achieved through optimization.
paper_structure: The paper presents a framework combining programmable integrated photonics with nonlinear fiber optics. The core methodology involves using machine learning to optimize the input pulse to sculpt the broadband supercontinuum output, which is then verified via high-speed optical characterization.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly controllable platform for generating complex light fields, which is fundamental for realizing advanced quantum light sources or performing complex nonlinear spectroscopy.

Figure 2 | Experimental setup for tailoring broadband and reconfigurable wavepackets. A signal processing stage first provides flexible control over a femtosecond input pulse train centred at 1550 nm through the use of an on-chip programmable delay line (PDL). The shaped pulse train is then amplified and launched into a highly nonlinear fibre (HNLF), where it undergoes nonlinear fibre propagation. The broadband wavepacket collected at the fibre output is a supercontinuum (SC) with controllable spectro-temporal properties.
